subject: Brightline MSA - Indemnity redlines and escrow/defense proposal
messages:
From: Michael Ross <michael.ross@brightline.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@brightline.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Brightline MSA - indemnity redlines (first pass)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attaching Brightline's redlines to the MSA and Order Form (Brightline_MSA_v3_redline.pdf). A few high‑level asks from our side on indemnity:

- Brightline needs a right to seek defense for third‑party IP claims that directly arise from Redwood's models as used by Brightline customers.
- If Redwood insists on "defend or reimburse" language, we need clarity on evidence and notice windows (we propose 45 days notice).
- Given the nature of model training data, Brightline prefers an escrow or holdback exhibit for IP indemnity remediation > $500k.

Can you confirm Redwood's starting position on: defense control, insurance offset, and whether escrow exhibit is something you can accept in principle?

We'd like to keep the procurement timeline tight — target signing within three weeks if possible. Happy to set up a short call this week to walk the redlines.

Best,
Michael Ross
VP Procurement, Brightline Health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Michael Ross <michael.ross@brightline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA - indemnity redlines (first pass)

Michael —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Ben from Legal Ops to propose specific language and an operational path for notice/evidence handling.

Quick answers up front:
- Defense control: Redwood is generally open to limited "defend" obligations for third‑party claims that arise solely from Redwood code or service defects, but we need to preserve the right to select counsel and manage settlement decisions for claims that implicate Redwood's broader platform or third‑party tech.
- Insurance offset: we will seek a standard insurance offset (we'll propose an insurance waterfall that avoids double recovery).
- Escrow/holdback: we're open to an escrow exhibit for large remediation events but need clear triggers, thresholds, and an operational owner for evidence/forensics.

Ben — attaching our quick internal checklist (indemnity-eval-checklist.docx) to frame the evidence we'll request if this moves to a defend request: notice template, sample logs, timeframe expectations, and escrow activation steps. Can you draft a counterproposal that:
  1) provides a compromise defense/control split,
  2) defines a $ threshold for escrow activation, and
  3) proposes a 30/45 day notice window we can live with?

Michael — would a 45‑minute sync tomorrow (Thu) at 10am ET work for you?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: indemnity-eval-checklist.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Michael Ross <michael.ross@brightline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA - indemnity redlines (first pass)

Michael / Tessa —

Appreciate the clarity. After quick review with Ops and Product, here's a pragmatic counterproposal we think will close:

1) Scope / Trigger
- Redwood will indemnify and "defend or, at Redwood's election, reimburse" Customer for third‑party claims alleging that Redwood's underlying service implementation (excluding customer prompts/data and third‑party datasets) directly infringes a third party's patent, copyright or trade secret.

2) Defense Control
- Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of Redwood's choice. If Redwood elects not to assume defense, Redwood will reimburse reasonable defense costs incurred by Customer, subject to approval of counsel rate reasonableness (can't be unbounded).

3) Escrow / Remediation Threshold
- For indemnity obligations that would reasonably require a remediation spend > $500,000, the parties agree to trigger the Escrow Exhibit (Proposed Exhibit E) for holdback of remediation funds or escrow arrangement. Exhibit defines trigger mechanics, release conditions, and dispute escalation path.

4) Notice & Cooperation
- Customer must provide written notice within 30 days of becoming aware of the claim, provide the evidence checklist Ben attached, and cooperate reasonably (testimony, limited access to relevant logs).

5) Insurance Offset & Caps
- Redwood proposes a mutual cap tied to the Order Form value (e.g., 150% of 12 months committed fees) for non‑willful infringement. Insurance proceeds may reduce Redwood's indemnity obligation (standard offsets apply).

6) Timing / Operational
- If Brightline accepts the threshold + exhibit approach, Redwood will prepare a clean counter‑redline of the MSA + Exhibit E and Proposed Exhibit E (proposed-escrow-exhibit.docx). We'll aim to circulate within 48 hours.

Inline, a short example redline we plan to propose: 
> "Redwood shall have the right to assume defense with counsel of Redwood's choice, provided Customer receives prompt notice and the opportunity to participate at its own expense; if Redwood declines defense, Redwood shall reimburse reasonable attorneys' fees incurred by Customer up to the deductible/cap."

Happy to jump on the call Tessa proposed — Ben (legal ops) will lead the redline deliverable and Laura is copied for exec sign‑off on escalation thresholds.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-escrow-exhibit.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Ross <michael.ross@brightline.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA - indemnity redlines (first pass) — Redwood counteroffer

Michael —

Thank you for the patience and the clear redlines. On behalf of Redwood leadership, I am authorized to present the following compromise as Redwood's commercial position. We view this as a balanced approach that preserves customer protections while protecting Redwood's platform and broader customers.

Proposal (summary):
- Defense/Control: Redwood will assume defense for claims that are limited to Redwood's service implementation; Redwood will select counsel and manage settlements. If Redwood elects not to defend, Redwood will reimburse Customer's reasonable, documented defense costs.
- Escrow/Threshold: An Escrow Exhibit (attached) will be added and will be triggered for aggregate remediation costs exceeding $500k. Exhibit defines holdback mechanics, release criteria, and a neutral technical arbitration path for disputed remediation scopes.
- Notice & Cooperation: 30 days' written notice preferred; minimal good‑faith cooperation is required (logs, point of contact).
- Cap & Insurance: For non‑willful infringement, cap = 150% of the annual committed fees under the applicable Order Form. Any applicable insurance proceeds will reduce Redwood's obligation.

Next steps:
1) Ben to produce a clean counter‑redline (M14) reflecting the above — delivered by Fri EOD PT.
2) If Brightline is comfortable with this framework, procurement to confirm escrow admin and we'll issue a DocuSign packet with the new Exhibit.
3) Tessa to coordinate a brief 30‑minute closing call next week to finalize.

We believe this closes the hard items and keeps the broader procurement timeline intact. If Brightline needs a different escrow administrator or alternate threshold, please flag that ASAP so we can evaluate.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
VP Legal & Compliance | Redwood Inference

--
Tessa / Ben — please proceed with the clean counter and send DocuSign link once procurement locks the escrow administrator.
